key_insight: The paper proposes Asymptotics Learning Theory, using linear least squares to recover unknown constants in asymptotic expansions with provable convergence-rate guarantees.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled numerical tool for estimating asymptotic parameters in scientific computing and combinatorics, complementing traditional ratio-based methods.
method: Sliding Linear Least Squares (sLLSQ) for estimating asymptotic constants from moving data windows.
Sliding Tikhonov Linear Least Squares (sT-LLSQ) to add regularization and improve stability.
Rigorous asymptotic analysis to derive sufficient convergence conditions and rate estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rigorous theory plus numerical examples that verify the convergence and convergence-rate claims across representative asymptotic settings.
watch_item: Both methods can converge slowly or even diverge in some cases, so window choice and regularization must be handled carefully.
paper_title: Learning Asymptotics with Convergence-Rate Guarantees using Linear Least Squares
